title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance targets, and a concise set of ADRs. It is intended as the single reference for engineering teams when designing new services, APIs, or model-serving deployments.

Scope: Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and all internal services that interact with inference runtime, control plane, telemetry, or provisioning systems.

Goals
- Provide consistent, secure, and maintainable APIs and codebases.
- Ensure predictable operational properties (latency, cost, reliability).
- Make model-serving safe, observable, and upgradeable across environments.
- Reduce onboarding friction and variance in infra patterns.

1) API Standards

Design Principles
- Consumer-first: design APIs for the developer experience (predictable error paths, helpful validation errors, clear pagination).
- Backwards-compatible by default: additive changes only; breakage requires versioned endpoints and an ADR.
- Secure by default: require auth, enforce least privilege, and default to denying unknown content.

Authentication & Authorization
- All public or cross-team endpoints must use JWTs signed by Redwood Auth (RS256) or mTLS for internal control-plane traffic.
- Scoped tokens: minimize scopes to required actions (e.g., inference:generate, models:read).
- Token rotation: rotation window <= 90 days for long-lived service tokens; short-lived tokens (<= 1h) for user requests.

Request/Response Contract
- Use JSON over HTTPS; content-type application/json.
- All API responses must include a top-level `meta` object with request_id, server_time_ms, and schema_version.
- Errors follow RFC 7807 (problem+json) with additional fields: error_code, retriable (bool), and docs_url.
- For streaming generation endpoints use server-sent events (SSE) or chunked Transfer-Encoding; include a final summary event with token_count and latency_ms.

Versioning
- Route versioning: /v1/..., /v2/... for user-facing endpoints. Minor/patch changes implemented via schema_version header.
- Deprecation policy: announce deprecations 60 days for non-breaking, 180 days for breaking changes with migration guide and sunset date.

Example endpoint (summary)
POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
Request body: {"model": "rwd-llm-7b", "input": "...", "max_tokens": 256} 
Response (200): {"meta": {"request_id": "r-123", "server_time_ms": 42}, "output": "..."}

2) Coding Standards

Languages & Tooling
- Primary languages: Go for control plane services, Rust/C++ for performance-critical runtime components, Python for experiments and evaluation harnesses.
- Supported language versions: Go 1.20+, Python 3.11+, Rust stable (latest).
- Enforce formatting: gofmt/gofumpt for Go, black/isort for Python, rustfmt for Rust.

Linters & Static Analysis
- Required linters: golangci-lint (Go), ruff/mypy (Python), clippy (Rust). CI must treat lint failures as build failures.
- Dependency scanning: Snyk or equivalent on every PR; high/critical findings must be triaged within 48 hours.

Testing & Coverage
- Unit tests for core logic; integration tests for service contracts.
- Minimum coverage target: 60% for libraries, 40% for services. Coverage gating is advisory for experimental repos and enforced for platform libraries.

Repository Layout & Modules
- One service per repository recommended. Shared libraries live in org-level modules with semantic versioning.
- Clear public/private API boundaries and CHANGELOG.md using Conventional Commits.

3) Infrastructure Standards

Accounts & Networking
- Environment separation: prod, staging, dev in separate cloud accounts/projects. No cross-environment credentials.
- VPC design: per-cluster subnets (control-plane, runtime, telemetry) with egress filtering.

Provisioning & IaC
- Terraform (>=1.5) for core infra; Terragrunt for composition allowed but discouraged for new projects.
- Module registry: all infra modules must be published and versioned.
- State management: remote state (S3/GCS) with state locking (DynamoDB/Cloud Storage locks).

Secrets & Key Management
- Secrets in HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS; no plaintext secrets in repos.
- Key rotation policy: KMS keys rotated annually; database credentials rotated every 90 days.

Tagging & Billing
- Required tags: owner_team, project, environment, cost_center. Tags used for billing exports.

4) Model-Serving Standards

Model Catalog & Metadata
- All models must be registered in the model catalog with: model_id, architecture, size, quantization_profile, supported_sequences, known_issues, benchmark_profiles.
- Metadata stored in a managed DB and exposed to runtime via versioned API.

Quantization & Variants
- Provide recommended quantization profiles per-model (fp16, int8, qat-int8) and measured perf/quality tradeoffs.
- Default routing: prefer quantized variant when latency/cost objectives are primary; fallback to full precision for quality-sensitive workloads.

Routing & Fallback Policies
- Smart routing rules: tag requests with latency_slo and cost_priority; router chooses variant and region.
- Fallback chain: primary variant -> compatible quantized variant -> regional replica -> queued or degraded response.

KV Cache & Batching
- KV cache retention policy: keep last 1k KV entries per session or 30 minutes, whichever comes first.
- Batching policy: continuous batching window 4-20ms for low-latency SLOs; longer windows for throughput-oriented routes.

Model Rollout & Canaries
- Canary policy: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated quality regressions checks (see Quality Guardrails folder). Each step 4 hours minimum and must pass latency and correctness gates.

5) Observability Standards

SLOs & Error Budgets
- Default SLOs for inference API (hosted): 99.5% p99 successful response < 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens); 99.9% availability for control plane. Dedicated/private SLOs negotiated per contract.
- Error budget burn policy: 7-day rolling window; escalations at 50% (pager), 80% (exec review).

Metrics & Instrumentation
- Expose metrics in Prometheus format. Required metrics: inference_latency_ms (histogram), tokens_generated_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio, active_sessions, model_load_time_ms, cpu_gpu_utilization_percent.
- Use semantic metric names and label cardinality limits (max 10 distinct label values per metric).

Tracing & Logs
- Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry. Trace sampling: 1% baseline, up to 100% for errors and pre-defined investments (incident investigations).
- Structured logs as JSON with fields: timestamp, level, service, request_id, trace_id, event, details. Logs should not contain PII.

Retention & Storage
- Metrics: 90 days at full resolution, 13 months aggregated. Traces: 30 days. Logs: 90 days for production; longer retention via premium add-on.

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarking

Latency & Throughput Targets
- Small workloads (<=128 tokens): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms (GPU-accelerated hosted runtime).
- Long generation (>512 tokens): throughput measured in tokens/sec per GPU; target baseline published in model catalog.

Benchmarking Suite
- Use the canonical benchmarking harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite). Bench jobs: unit perf tests (PR gated), nightly fleet-wide benchmarks, regional capacity reports.
- Key benchmarks: cold model load, steady-state throughput, KV cache hit impact, quantization accuracy vs baseline.

Optimization & Cost Controls
- Recommend batching and KV caching profiles per workload; provide autosuggested configs in Redwood Optimize.
- Baseline P50 cost-per-token target for common models stored in model catalog; use as guardrail when recommending quantization.

7) Decision Records (ADRs) - canonical list
- ADR-2024-01: Runtime language choice - Adopted Rust for low-level runtime components (link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture).
- ADR-2025-03: Default auth model - Use RS256 JWTs with short-lived access tokens.
- ADR-2025-07: Quantization strategy - Standardize on int8 optimized kernels with fp16 fallback for high-quality routes.
- ADR-2026-01: Telemetry retention - Metrics 90d, traces 30d, logs 90d (this doc references enforcement controls).

Each ADR includes: decision, status, alternatives considered, consequences, and date. New ADRs are added under architecture-and-standards/decision-records and require at least two engineering reviewers.

8) Governance, Ownership, and Change Process

Ownership
- Architecture and Standards owner: Architecture Council (rotating chairs from Eng Platform and Eng SRE).
- Day-to-day owner: Architecture Guild (owner_team == engineering).

Change Process (high level)
1. Proposer drafts change and files a PR against this canonical doc or creates a new ADR if it is a significant architectural change.
2. Seek at least two reviewers from different teams (e.g., runtime and infra).
3. Run the change through the compatibility checklist (backwards compatibility, infra impact, cost estimate).
4. Approval: minor non-breaking changes approved by Architecture Guild; breaking or cross-cutting changes require Architecture Council approval and a communicated rollout plan.

Escalation & Rollout
- Major infra or API changes require a rollout plan (canary cadence, rollback criteria, communication plan) and a post-rollout verification runbook.
- Rollbacks: target recovery RTO <= 30 minutes for control-plane regressions; document the rollback playbook in runbooks/ under eng-platform.

Appendix: Key Config & SLO Table

+-------------------------------+-------------------------------+
| Item                          | Requirement / Threshold       |
+-------------------------------+-------------------------------+
| Inference p99 latency (short) | < 300ms                       |
| Availability (control plane)  | 99.9%                         |
| Metrics retention             | 90 days (full), 13 months agg |
| Traces retention              | 30 days                       |
| Model canary cadence          | 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%      |
| KV cache retention            | 30 minutes or last 1k entries |
+-------------------------------+-------------------------------+

Appendix: Quickcheck PR checklist
- API: schema and version changes documented; client migration notes included.
- Security: threat model updated; no secrets in code.
- Observability: metrics/traces/logs added for new endpoints.
- Performance: include simple micro-benchmark results where appropriate.
- Testing: unit + integration + canary plan.
